product_brief: Enterprise server platform with Common Cryptographic Architecture (CCA) 8.4 supporting ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and RSA 8K.
pqc_capability_description: CCA 8.4 adds support for ML-KEM (NIST FIPS 203) for key encapsulation and ML-DSA (NIST FIPS 204) for digital signatures. Supports ML-DSA pure and pre-hash keys, deterministic/non-deterministic signatures, and ML-KEM key generation/encapsulation/decapsulation. Available on IBM z17 and z16.
crypto_primitives: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, RSA (up to 8192-bit), AES, TDES
key_management_model: Hardware-backed key storage via IBM CEX8S (4770) cryptographic coprocessor; secure key generation and management via CCA APIs and ICSF; supports skeleton key tokens and clear key formats.
architecture_type: Hardware-based cryptographic coprocessor (IBM CEX8S) integrated into IBM z17/z16 mainframe servers; on-prem appliance/server form factor.
fips_validated: Not stated (References NIST FIPS 203 and FIPS 204 standards for algorithms, but does not state FIPS 140-2/3 validation status for the module itself)
pqc_roadmap_details: CCA 8.4 introduces ML-KEM and ML-DSA support; also available on IBM z16.
testing_&_validation_methods: Supports running NIST Known Answer Tests (KATs) for ML-DSA and ML-KEM using ACVP-Server vectors; includes RAWSEED rule for testing.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Requires ICSF exploitation APAR OA66395 (HCR77D2 - 77E0) and toleration APAR OA66396; requires CCA firmware version 8.4 on IBM CEX8S hardware.

product_brief: Enterprise server platform and operating system requiring PQC migration for cryptographic security.
pqc_capability_description: The document states that "PQC Migration implications for IBM Z and z/OS" are a topic of discussion. It notes that replacing public-key systems will take 5 to 15 years and that sensitive data is at risk now. It mentions NIST PQC standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205) and that IBM developed three of the first four algorithms selected by NIST. It does not state that PQC is currently implemented or available in production on IBM Z/z/OS, but rather that migration is necessary and planned.
crypto_primitives: RSA, DSA, ECDSA, ECDH, DES, TDES, AES, SHA-256, SHA-3
target_industries: Enterprise, Financial Systems, Critical Infrastructure, Government (implied by RACF Users Group and enterprise context)
pqc_roadmap_details: Replacing public-key systems will take 5 to 15 years. NIST released initial final standards in 2024. IBM developed three of the first four NIST-selected algorithms (CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium, and one other implied partner). FALCON draft standard planned for 2025. HQC selected as additional PQC algorithm in 2025.
signature_schemes: Current: RSA, DSA, ECDSA. Planned/Standardized: ML-DSA (CRYSTALS-Dilithium), SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+), FALCON (planned 2025).
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Replacing most public-key systems will take 5 to 15 years.
organizational_readiness: Start your quantum safe journey now; sensitive data generated today is at risk.
